**2. Where L lies.** Because C lies on EB and D lies on EA, ∠CED = ∠BEA. The bisector of this angle meets AB at a point L with AL/LB = EA/EB. Coordinates confirm that the E-excenter of ECD lies on AB (its y-coordinate is about 0), so L is this point, as the solution claims.

**3. Computing OL.** Let u = EC, v = ED, t = CD/20. Similarity of ECD and EAB gives u = t(v+7) and v = t(u+13). Solving, u − v = −6t/(1+t) and u + v = 20t/(1−t). Since OL = 10|u − v|/(u + v), this gives OL = 3(1−t)/(1+t). Substituting t = (9√1001 − 91)/400 and rationalizing gives OL = (97 − 3√1001)/2.
